title: A skate rack from CAD to plywood

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Skateboards leaning in every corner. A landlord who doesn't want holes in the walls. What do you do?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine designed one. In December 2021 he modelled a vertical rack in CAD and built it from plywood, to hold skateboards and a snowboard without drilling into rental walls.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Six or more boards, so six slots per side panel. Snowboard plus skates, so a taller top bay. Freestanding, no lag bolts. And cheap: three-quarter inch plywood, screws and stain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two side panels, three horizontal ties, and angled slots so decks slide in and stay put. He aimed for roughly a fifteen to twenty degree downward angle, and a panel height around six feet so the snowboard fits.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: But there was a detour, I read.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A welded tubular orange frame, built in a school shop. Good practice for squareness, but too heavy and too industrial for a bedroom. It still proved the layout of posts and cross-members.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Home Depot run, then slots cut with a spade bit, a circular saw and a file. He stained it in a cold garage, and a cat inspected the quality on every flat surface.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. Next time he'd use a steeper slot angle for longboards, edge banding on the slot mouths, and a French cleat wall mount when he's not renting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The full write-up has the CAD render and the build photos.
